plan.title: Silent on a rest-day Sunday: the 6 pm recap as its own text, then a reply leads into the week talk

context.text: THREE minutes, Sam. That's real. Sunday's a rest day, back at it Monday.

transcript.text:
Hey Sam! Here's the progress you made this week:

• 5 step days done in full and 1 smaller version, with a Strava screenshot for every one of them
• Your jog intervals grew from 1 minute on Monday to 3 minutes straight on Saturday
• On Tuesday you slowed to a pace where you could talk, and that made the run doable
• Saturday's run was 1.0 mi on Strava, so you've covered a mile with walk breaks mixed in

Your goal is a mile without stopping by Nov 14. You've got 3 straight minutes of jogging down, and the next step is stretching those jogs longer. What do you want to push on this week: longer jogs, or fewer walk breaks?

It should feel huge, Sam. A week ago a single minute was hard, and now you're at three. That's the proof your body is adapting. 🙌

Tomorrow we build on it. Around the block at 6:30 pm, 4 min jog, 1 min walk, 3 rounds, same talk-test pace. Send a Strava screenshot after. Work for you?
keep building toward the mile, maybe 4 min jogs?

Locked in, Sam. 4 min jogs it is, and that's exactly the right way to build toward your mile. Tomorrow at 6:30 pm: 4 min jog, 1 min walk, 3 rounds, talk-test pace, around the block. Strava screenshot after. Let's go. 💪
Let's go, Sam. Monday, 6:30 pm, 4 min jogs around the block. You've got this. 🔥

checks.reason: Four backed bullets (5 full and 1 smaller, 1 min to 3 min jogs, talk-test pace, 1.0 mi) framed as progress, then one question about the week.
Claims no understanding; the shin lesson is not mentioned and the talk-test lesson is only described as what made the run doable.
Every number and detail matches the step log and proof: 1 min to 3 min jogs, 1.0 mi Saturday, 5 full and 1 smaller day.
No 'unprompted' or 'on your own' wording about a lesson.
Recap runs about 7 short lines with one question at the end, within the recap allowance.
Warm, direct, one emoji-free text, no overfamiliarity.
Not applicable: the Sunday was not quiet, so this check does not apply.
'That's the proof your body is adapting' is a physical claim, not a claim of understanding; acceptable.
Monday's 1 min jog being hard matches the log ('harder than expected'); the step matches the plan.
Several sentences, but it sets a fully defined step, which allows a longer presenting text.
Pushy-level energy, sincere, one emoji as punctuation.
Restates the full step after the tester's change; a repeat of a settled step, though brief.
Warm and hype-level appropriate, one emoji at the end.
Two short sentences, no question, as required after 'perfect'.
Short, warm confirmation with one emoji at the end.

conversation.reason: The week recap arrives as its own 6 pm text on a silent Sunday, and the reply turns to the week with substance first.
ZOH answers the tester's 'felt huge' with substance (adaptation, the week's growth) before the next step.
Monday's step is defined (what, where, when) and asked if it works, but no explicit length (about 15 min) is given.
Opens with name, recap with backed progress, mile status, one question, no proof ask, and a confirmation after 'perfect'; the step omits the explicit length.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the 6 pm week recap well: grounded, short, backed by the record, with a mile status and one question, and it avoided overclaiming the shin lesson. The weaker spots are that the Monday step never states its length and the step is restated after the tester's change without a clear yes.
